question: How many Japanese prefectures will report 10.00 or more influenza cases per sentinel site in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's Week 50 2026 report?

calls.reasoning: Week 45 (Nov 2-8): national 11.00 (up from 10.26, 3rd straight rise), 23 prefectures >=10 (Hokkaido + 22). Rise concentrated in north/east (Hokkaido 28.32, Fukushima 21.08), while west/Kyushu are declining (Ehime fell from 27.89 to 17.71). A(H1N1)pdm09 dominant. Five weeks to Week 50: December seasonality favors growth and a jump to 35-47 prefectures, but an early wave peaking (as in 2025/26, which peaked in Week 47) could cut the count to around 10. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi.
calls.dossier:
- MHLW Week 45 2026 (Nov 2-8; released Nov 13): national 11.00 per sentinel site, up from 10.26 in Week 44; 3rd straight weekly increase after a temporary dip in Week 42 (Resemom/Nikkei Medical, 2026-11-13).
- Week 45: Hokkaido + 22 prefectures = 23 prefectures at advisory level (>=10); 34 prefectures rose week on week (ANN/KSB, 2026-11-13). Resemom says 33 rose, 14 fell.
- Week 45 top values: Hokkaido 28.32, Fukushima 21.08 (from 13.77), Aomori 19.79, Iwate 19.74, Miyagi 18.45, Yamagata 18.36, Ehime 17.71, Akita 16.56; lowest Kagawa 3.96 (Resemom, Weathernews 2026-11-13).
- Ehime led in Week 44 at 27.89, then dropped; western Japan and Kyushu-Okinawa mostly declining, north/east rising (Resemom, Nikkei Medical 2026-11-13). Tokyo, Aichi, Osaka, Fukuoka flat (tenki.jp 2026-11-14).
- Aomori: 9 consecutive weekly rises, 19.79 in Week 45 (Web Toho 2026-11-13).
- Week 45 total reports 41,071, about half last year's level for the same week and about 8x two years earlier (Weathernews).
- Subtype: A(H1N1)pdm09 reported dominant (~97% of detections since summer 2026, per web summary of clinic/society material); last strongly H1-dominated season was 2019/20 (national peak ~18 at Week 52). 2025/26 was an H3N2 subclade K wave peaking around Week 47 (~51 nationally), then a B wave.
- Holidays: Week 45 contains Nov 3; Week 47 contains Nov 23 (Monday); Week 50 = Dec 7-13 with no holiday.
- Mapping: national 11.00 corresponds to 23 prefectures >=10; historically a national rate of ~20+ tends to put most prefectures (35-45+) above 10, while ~6-8 nationally corresponds to roughly 8-15.
- Status quo: if levels persist, the count stays in the low-to-mid 20s.
- Resolves off the MHLW influenza press release for Week 50 (count of prefectures with per-sentinel value >=10.00); JIHS IDWR is the backup source.
- Event window: the single Week 50 report (Dec 7-13, 2026, published ~Dec 18); as of Nov 14, Week 45 is the latest data, 5 reporting weeks remain.
- Not found: exact Week 44 prefecture count; full prefecture table (PDF not parseable); Week 46 data; any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi).

calls.reasoning: Week 45: national rate 11.00, 23 prefectures at 10+ (Week 44: 19; Week 41: 29). H1N1pdm09 wave that started early and has plateaued at ~9-13 since early October, growing in Hokkaido/Tohoku and declining in western Japan. With 5 weeks to Week 50 (Dec 7-13), December seasonality and cold air from Nov 19 favor moderate growth into the high 20s/30s; regional burnout could pull the count back to the teens. Above 40 prefectures needs a national rate of ~25+, which is less likely in an H1 season that has plateaued. No human market found (per runs and harness; no web access this run).
calls.reconciliation: The three dossiers agree on every factual point: Week 45 at 11.00 with 23 prefectures, Week 44 at 10.26 (Run 3 reports 19 prefectures; nothing contradicts it), Week 41 at 12.81 with 29, H1N1 dominant, north/east rising and west falling. Nothing factual needed settling. The only disagreement was a judgment call on mass above 40 prefectures (Runs 1/2/3: 20%/9%/15%). I put it at ~13%: reaching that needs a national rate of ~25+ by Week 50, which is less likely given the 6-week plateau and the mild mid-December 2019/20 H1 analog, but possible given December seasonality and the H1 immunity gap. I agree with and keep Run 3's interior shape and dispersion (~26). No web access this run, so no market check of my own; runs and harness found none.
